topics.title: The day the tank went dry

learn.hook: Imagine opening the tap to brush your teeth... and nothing comes out! Let's read about a street where that happened.
points: A story has a setting (where and when), characters (who) and a problem.
Look for clue words that tell when: 'one hot May morning', 'at noon', 'that evening'.
Look for the cause of the problem: why did something happen?
Sound words like 'drip, drip, drip' help us hear the story.
A good story often ends with a lesson the characters learn.

example.q: Read: One hot May morning, the taps in Gully No. 4 went dry. 'The tank on the roof is empty!' shouted Bunty. Everyone went up to the terrace to look. A pipe had been leaking all night, drip, drip, drip. A plumber fixed the pipe, and a water tanker came at noon. That evening, the children made a poster: 'Every drop counts! Close the tap!' Why did the taps go dry?
steps: Find the problem: the taps went dry and the tank was empty.
Find the cause: 'A pipe had been leaking all night'.
So the water slowly ran out through the leak.
example.answer: Because a pipe had been leaking all night and the tank became empty.

learn.reallife: In many Indian towns, water comes at fixed times and is stored in tanks. A small leak can waste a lot of it, so we must report leaks quickly.

games.title: True or false? (from the story)
items: The story happens on a hot May morning.
The tank was on the roof.
Bunty shouted, 'The tank on the roof is empty!'
The water tanker came at midnight.
The children made a poster about saving water.
It said, 'Every drop counts! Close the tap!'

games.title: Story order
games.prompt: Put the story events in order
items: Bunty finds the tank is empty.

quiz.q: Read: 'One hot May morning, the taps in Gully No. 4 went dry.' When did the taps go dry?
quiz.explain: The line says 'One hot May morning'.
quiz.mistake: Does not find the time words in the line

quiz.q: Read: 'A pipe had been leaking all night, drip, drip, drip.' Why was the tank empty?
options: A pipe had been leaking all night
quiz.explain: The leak let the water drip out all night until the tank was empty.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a reason instead of finding it in the story

quiz.q: Read: 'A plumber fixed the pipe, and a water tanker came at noon.' Who fixed the pipe?
quiz.explain: The line clearly says a plumber fixed the pipe.
quiz.mistake: Picks a character without checking the line

quiz.q: Read: 'A plumber fixed the pipe, and a water tanker came at noon.' When did the water tanker come?
quiz.explain: Noon means twelve o'clock in the daytime.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'noon'

quiz.q: Read: 'A pipe had been leaking all night, drip, drip, drip.' What do the words 'drip, drip, drip' tell us?
options: Water was falling drop by drop
quiz.explain: 'Drip' is the sound of single drops falling, again and again.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a leak must be a big gush

quiz.q: Read: 'The children made a poster: 'Every drop counts! Close the tap!'' What was the poster about?
quiz.explain: 'Every drop counts' and 'Close the tap' are about saving water.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the poster's words

quiz.q: What does 'Every drop counts' mean?
options: Even a little water is important
quiz.explain: It means even small amounts of water matter, so we should not waste any.
quiz.mistake: Takes the words 'counts' literally

quiz.q: Read: ''The tank on the roof is empty!' shouted Bunty.' Where was the water tank?
quiz.explain: Bunty says 'The tank on the roof'.
quiz.mistake: Does not find the place word in the line

teach.ask: Gappu drinks from a puddle: 'Why did the tank go dry? What did the children learn?'
teach.praise: Drip, drip, hooray! You explained it so well!
teach.nudge: What caused the tank to go empty? And what lesson did the children share?

learn.hook: 'Close the tap!' 'Fix the leak!' Instructions are short and bossy... but they help save water!
points: An instruction tells someone what to do. It often begins with an action word: Close, Turn, Use, Fix.
To say what not to do, begin with 'Do not' or 'Don't': Don't leave the tap running.
Add 'Please' to make an instruction polite: Please turn off the tap.
Ways to save water: turn off the tap while brushing, use a bucket to bathe, fix leaks, reuse water for plants.
Rainwater harvesting means collecting rainwater and storing it to use later.

example.q: Change into an instruction: 'You should turn off the tap while brushing your teeth.'
steps: An instruction starts with the action word.
example.answer: Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth.

learn.reallife: School posters, recipe steps and game rules are full of instructions. Writing your own 'Save Water' rules for home is a great project!

games.title: Save or waste?
items: Turning off the tap while brushing
Watering plants with water used to wash vegetables
Washing a scooter with a running pipe

quiz.q: Which sentence is an instruction?
quiz.explain: It tells someone what to do and begins with an action word.
quiz.mistake: Picks a telling or asking sentence

quiz.q: Which is a good tip for saving water?
options: Leave the tap on while brushing.
Use a bucket and mug to bathe.
Let the tank overflow every day.
Wash the floor with a running pipe.
quiz.explain: A bucket helps us use only the water we need.
quiz.mistake: Does not see which habit wastes water

quiz.q: Most instructions begin with ___.
quiz.explain: Instructions usually start with a verb like close, use or fix.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the shape of an instruction

quiz.q: Which instruction tells what NOT to do?
quiz.explain: 'Don't' tells someone not to do something.
quiz.mistake: Misses the word 'Don't'

quiz.q: What is rainwater harvesting?
options: Collecting and storing rainwater to use later
quiz.explain: We collect rainwater from roofs and store it in tanks or let it soak into the ground.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'harvesting' must be about crops

quiz.q: Ammi washed the vegetables in a bowl. What is the best use of that leftover water?
quiz.explain: Reusing clean leftover water for plants saves fresh water.
quiz.mistake: Does not think of reusing water

quiz.q: Which instruction is the most polite?
quiz.explain: 'Please' makes an instruction polite.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a short, loud order is polite

quiz.q: Which habit does NOT save water?
options: Washing a car with a running pipe
Turning off the tap while soaping
quiz.explain: A running pipe wastes a lot of water. A bucket uses much less.
quiz.mistake: Misreads 'NOT' in the question

teach.ask: Gappu sprinkles water everywhere: 'Oops! How do I give an instruction to save water?'
teach.praise: Close the tap! See? I can give instructions too! Thank you!
teach.nudge: How does an instruction begin? And how can we make it polite?

topics.title: Compound words: two words become one

learn.hook: Rain + water = rainwater. Sun + flower = sunflower. Two small words can join to make a brand-new word!
points: A compound word is made by joining two words: rain + coat = raincoat.
The two parts often give a clue to the meaning: a toothbrush is a brush for teeth.
Some compound words have a new meaning: a butterfly is not made of butter!
Home words: bathroom, rooftop, teapot, bedroom.

example.q: Which two words make 'rainwater', and what does it mean?
steps: Put the meanings together: water that comes from the rain.
example.answer: rain + water: water from the rain

learn.reallife: Look around your home: bedroom, toothpaste, cupboard, doorbell. Compound words are everywhere!

quiz.q: Which is a compound word?
quiz.explain: Toothbrush is made of two words: tooth + brush.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a word with an ending like -ing is a compound word

quiz.q: sun + light = ?
quiz.explain: Joining sun and light gives sunlight.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with only one of the parts

quiz.q: Which two words make 'bathroom'?
quiz.explain: 'Bathroom' is a room for taking a bath: bath + room.
quiz.mistake: Splits the word in the wrong place

quiz.q: Which word can join 'foot' to make a compound word?
quiz.explain: Foot + ball = football.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that does not make a real word

quiz.q: What is a 'waterfall'?
options: A glass of water that fell
quiz.explain: A waterfall is water flowing down from a high place, like a cliff.
quiz.mistake: Does not combine the meanings of the two parts

quiz.q: Which is NOT a compound word?
quiz.explain: 'Bucket' cannot be split into two words. The others can: roof + top, tea + pot, sun + flower.
quiz.mistake: Splits a word into pieces that are not real words

quiz.q: roof + top = ?
quiz.explain: Joining roof and top gives rooftop, the top of a roof.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that only sounds similar

quiz.q: A pot for making tea is a ___.
quiz.explain: Tea + pot = teapot.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with only one part of the meaning

teach.ask: Gappu tries: 'Bird + house = birdhouse? What is a compound word?'
teach.praise: Yes! Birdhouse is a compound word, and now I am super-happy!
teach.nudge: How is a compound word made? Can you give me an example?
